neighbours.label: the verb ' means' / ' mean' / ' meant' in 'X means Y' (this implies / entails)
fire: Moving to the coast also means we will see our grandchildren more often.
A late frost can mean the loss of the entire apple harvest.
Being a good editor means cutting the sentences you love most.
Winning tonight would mean a place in the national final for the club.
For many families, a closed bridge means an extra hour of driving.
Owning a dog means walking it twice a day, whatever the weather.
The red light on the panel means the battery needs charging.
Higher interest rates mean that many buyers can no longer afford a house.
quiet: Moving to the coast will also bring us closer to our grandchildren.
A late frost can destroy the entire apple harvest in a single night.
A good editor cuts the sentences she loves most without hesitation.
Winning tonight would give the club a place in the national final.
For many families, a closed bridge adds an extra hour of driving.
Owning a dog requires walking it twice a day, whatever the weather.
The red light on the panel shows that the battery needs charging.
Higher interest rates make houses unaffordable for many buyers.
